Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! India have a daunting task ahead of them. The Indian players are in the huddle before they spread out. England Women openers, Tammy Beaumont and Danni Wyatt also walk out to the middle now. Jhulan Goswami to start with the ball for India Women. How will England Women approach this? Let's find out. Here we go...
...THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, England need just 135 to win this game and they would be looking to do that as quickly as possible. The pitch has no demons in it and anything other than a victory for England Women will be a big surprise. Can India Women pull off a miracle here? We shall find out. Stay tuned for the run-chase!

Meanwhile, Nasser Hussain is giving a pitch update. He calls it an absolute belter and reckons that all the English bowlers did was to pitch it fuller. Informs that there is no rough at all and it wasn't spinning square. How did Charlotte Dean take a 4-fer then? Nasser feels that she used her index finger beautifully to get the ball to drift. Adds that she was not imparting great spin and only deceiving the batters with her drift by using the breeze. Nasser Hussain further states that India's hopes will be on Sneh Rana as she also gets beautiful under-cut on her deliveries and will be important during the chase.

Charlotte Dean (8.2-1-23-4) gets her career-best figures and comes up for a quick word. Says that her plan was to vary her lengths and keep it in the line of the stumps. Adds that it has not been the World Cup they'd imagined but this performance will keep them going for the rest of the games.

Indian batters just couldn't handle the pressure put by the English bowlers with their tight lines and lengths. They lost early wickets and never recovered after that. Smriti Mandhana was the lone warrior as Harmanpreet Kaur failed to support her today. Eventually, she too departed and it was only because of a brief partnership between Richa Ghosh and Jhulan Goswami, India managed to reach 134. Things look bleak for them now and unless there is a special performance with the ball by someone, it seems very difficult for India Women to win from here.

A lot of eyebrows were raised when England Women decided to bowl first on this pitch. However, they have answered their critics in style with a clinical bowling performance. Anya Shrubsole seems to have started from the World Cup final of the last edition as she took two early wickets to put India on the back foot. The fielding was also top-notch and that brought two run-outs for them. This venue has been most helpful for the spinners and the English spinners took full advantage of it. Charlotte Dean got two wickets in one over and that broke the backbone of the Indian batting line-up. She eventually got four wickets and was ably supported by Sophie Ecclestone. This is a dominating performance and they would look to finish the chase as quickly as possible to boost their NRR.

A fantastic bowling performance by England Women! They were under the pump with three losses in the first three games but have made a strong statement with a strong bowling performance here. India Women, on the other hand, will be mighty disappointed with their batting performance as the conditions were pretty good to bat on and they need a miracle now to win this game from here. This is also India’s lowest total in the last four World Cups.

OUT! BOWLED! Dean finished with four wickets in the match. Loopy and full, around off and drifting in, Meghna Singh goes down to sweep but is early into the shot. It goes through to shatter the stumps and India Women are bowled out for 134.
Fuller and on middle, it's flicked through square leg for a single.
Short and cut through point for two.
Wide! Skidding down the leg side, Singh tries to tuck it away but misses.
Loopy and full around middle, defended back.
Fires it full around off, Meghna Singh defends off the front foot.
Leans forward and defends a full ball to the off side.
Shorter and around off, Singh plays it down to point.
Flighted and on middle, defended on the leg side.
Sophie Ecclestone is back on.
Tossed up nicely, outside off. Rajeshwari Gayakwad leaves it alone.
Very slow again and slightly shorter on middle. Singh pulls it to fine leg for a single.
Again tossed up on off. Singh pushes it towards the off side.
Tossed up on off. Singh blocks it out.
Slower in the air, on middle. Singh works it towards the leg side.
Slower in the air, outside off. Singh leaves it alone.
On a length, on off. Rajeshwari Gayakwad blocks it out.
Rajeshwari Gayakwad is the number 11 batter.

OUT! TAKEN! Jhulan Goswami departs now and India on the brink of getting bowled out here! A length delivery, outside off. Jhulan Goswami drives it on up and away from her body. The ball catches the thick outside edge of her blade and goes towards point. Danni Wyatt there takes a simple catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Danni Wyatt b Kate Cross

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten again! This is on a good length and outside off. Jhulan Goswami looks to punch it towards the off sider again but misses.
Play and a miss! A good-length delivery, around off. Jhulan Goswami looks to punch it towards the off side but misses.
Wide called for height! Bouncer on middle, over the head. Amy Jones, standing up to the stumps, takes it well.
FOUR! Smashed! A touch short in length, around off, Jhulan Goswami hangs back inside the crease and smacks it past the diving mid off fielder for a boundary.
Wide! Down the leg side, Jhulan Goswami tries to flick but misses.
Meghna Singh walks in next.

OUT! RUN OUT! This is the last thing India needed, Ghosh was playing well but has thrown it away in a bid to steal a needless run. Fuller delivery on middle. Jhulan Goswami works it towards mid-wicket. There is no single available but Ghosh searches for it and comes running down the track, Jhulan Goswami sends her back and rightly so. Natalie Sciver there is quick to collect the ball and fires a direct hit at the bowler's end as Ghosh puts in a dive. The appeal is made and the decision is taken upstairs. The replays show that Richa's bat is not grounded and we can see the shadow. One of the bails is off at that time. There goes India's final hope of getting to a challenging total.
Appeal for a run out! It's a direct hit at the bowler's end. Has the dive saved Richa Ghosh? No. The bat is in the air, one can see the shadow when the bails came off.
Slightly shorter on off. Jhulan Goswami punches this to the left of mid off for a single.
Slower and tossed up on middle again. Jhulan Goswami works it towards the leg side but fails to find the gap again.
Goes fuller on middle this time. Jhulan Goswami pushes it to mid-wicket.
This is short and wide outside off. Ghosh cuts it to deep point for a single.
Slower in the air again, on middle. Jhulan Goswami pushes it to long on for a single.
Slower in the air, on middle. Jhulan Goswami works it towards mid-wicket.

Drinks break. Some exceptional bowling in the middle overs by England Women, especially the spinners, has handed the advantage to the defending champions.​ India Women have lost the cream of their batting and have only Richa Ghosh as the last recognized batter. Jhulan Goswami is offering her good support as they aim to get to a challenging total. Still, 18 overs left in the innings and if India Women bat the distance, which looks unlikely at the moment, they will set a handy target. Heather Knight to bowl after the break...
A length delivery on middle. Ghosh works it towards the leg side this time. Dot to end the over but still a very good one for India, 12 off it.

FOUR! India are showing the intent and these are crucial runs! Length delivery on off. Ghosh walks down the track and looks to heave it towards the leg side. She gets the thick outside edge and the ball races away towards the third man fence for a boundary.
On a length and around off. Jhulan Goswami guides it towards third man for a single.
SIX! Up and over and dismissed! Jhulan Goswami showing her experience there! Length delivery, around off, Jhulan uses her long reach and dismisses it behind the bowler for a biggie.
On a length, around off. Jhulan Goswami defends it towards the off side.
On middle and fuller. Ghosh works it towards the leg side and they take a quick single. The fielder there runs in and throws at the batter's end but misses.
A fuller delivery on off. Jhulan Goswami pushes it to covers this time.
FOUR! This will give more confidence to India and Jhulan Goswami! Tossed up on off. Jhulan Goswami stays deep in her crease and forces it past mid on for a boundary.
It's pushed quicker on off. Jhulan Goswami drives it to covers.
This is fuller again, on off. Ghosh drives it to sweeper cover for a single.
Loopy delivery on off again. Ghosh drives it to mid off this time.
Tossed up on middle. Ghosh works it towards mid-wicket.
On a good length around off, Richa Ghosh steers it behind point for a run. 30 overs gone, India Women are 103/7!
Delivers it very full and outside off, it's driven to the cover fielder.

FOUR! Good attempt by Dean but it's a boundary. 100 up for India Women! Fuller and around off, Richa Ghosh steps back to make room and lofts it over mid off. Charlotte Dean gives the chase, does well to pull it back as well but the ball again rolls back to find the fence.
Fuller and on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Around off, on a length and skidding in, Ghosh defends it from the back foot to covers.
Around off, on a length, Ghosh pushes it from the back foot to covers and looks for a run. She is sent back by Jhulan.
Sophie Ecclestone is given a break and Kate Cross is brought into the attack.
Flatter and shorter on off, Richa Ghosh goes on the back foot and punches it to sweeper cover for one.
Too full and around off, Richa drives it back and the bowler collects it with a dive to her right.
Quicker and fuller, worked behind square leg for a run.
Fuller and on off, Jhulan Goswami forces it down to mid on, again.
Flighted and around middle, Jhulan Goswami eases her drive past the bowler but finds mid on.
Tossed up around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Fuller and around off, Jhulan drives it to short cover where the fielder makes a half stop and parries it to mid off. They cross.
Fullish and around leg, Jhulan Goswami helps it to short mid-wicket.
Fuller and close to off, Jhulan Goswami drives but finds mid off.
Fires it in, very full and around middle, Jhulan tries to drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads as the ball rolls back to Sophie Ecclestone.
Very full and around leg, Jhulan drives it back to the bowler.
A touch short and on off, Richa gets back and punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
A fuller delivery on off. Ghosh pushes it towards the off side and takes a single.
Tossed up nicely on off. Ghosh skips down the track but defends it as she fails to reach the pitch of the ball.
A flatter delivery on  middle. Ghosh works it towards the leg side this time.
Pushed quicker on off. Ghosh drives it to covers again.
This is fuller on off. Ghosh drives it to the cover fielder in the ring.
Dean goes quicker on off. Ghosh looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge towards backward point.
A low full toss around off, it's eased to the left of mid off for a quick run.
FOUR! Fine shot! Full and floated around middle, Richa Ghosh walks down the track, makes room and lofts it over extra cover for a boundary.
Too full and on middle, once again Richa drives it back to Sophie Ecclestone.
Fuller and on middle, driven back to the bowler.
Shortish and on off, Richa goes back and pushes it off the bottom half to mid off.
Full and around off, pushed to covers.
Goes fuller on off. Ghosh works it through square leg and takes a single.
A quicker delivery on off. Ghosh blocks this off the front foot.
Flatter and quicker on middle. Jhulan Goswami works it left of square leg for a single.
Jhulan Goswami is the new batter.

OUT! LBW! Charlotte Dean eventually has her third wicket of the match. She was denied last time but not this time. This is fuller but on middle on this occasion. Pooja Vastrakar looks to work it towards the leg side in her unusual way. She is half down to sweep but misses it again. The ball hits her pads and again the finger goes up from the umpire. Pooja Vastrakar take the review. The replays roll in and the UltraEdge shows no bat involved. The Ball Tracking shows three reds so Pooja Vastrakar has to walk back this time. India Women continue with their downward slide.
The batter has just watchfully blocked this out.

NOT OUT! Good suggestion by Richa Ghosh to take the review and Pooja Vastrakar survives. This one lands around off and Pooja Vastrakar looks to paddle it but misses. The ball hits her pads and there is an appeal. The umpire raises the finger and Pooja Vastrakar takes a late review. The Ball Tracking shows that the impact is outside off, so the decision will be overturned and Pooja Vastrakar can continue.
Late review. Pooja Vastrakar is adjudged lbw. She starts to walk but her partner suggests taking the DRS. Whoa! The impact is outside off and Pooja Vastrakar survives.
A flatter delivery on middle. Ghosh blocks it out.
FOUR! This time she finds the gap and two boundaries in two overs for her. Short and wide outside off. Ghosh rocks back and cuts it through backward point for a boundary.
Slight mix-up there! A fuller delivery around off. Ghosh pushes it towards covers and looks for a single but is sent back by her partner.
Slower in the air, on middle. Ghosh works it towards mid-wicket.
Slightly shorter on off. Pooja Vastrakar goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a single.
Tossed up, on off. Pooja Vastrakar defends this off the front foot.
A flatter delivery on off. Ghosh defends it towards the off side.

FOUR! This time Ghosh goes for a big shot and connects it quite well. This is tossed up on off. Ghosh shimmies down the track and slams it over mid off for a boundary. She now has the license to play her natural game.
Just over the fielder this time! This is on off and fuller. Pooja Vastrakar looks to go big downtown and ends up slicing it over extra-cover for a single.
Slower again, on off. Ghosh gets forward and works it behind square leg for a single.
Tossed up on off this time. Pooja Vastrakar works it towards the backward square leg region for a single.
Darted on leg. Pooja Vastrakar paddle-sweeps it towards fine leg for a couple.
A flatter delivery on off. Ghosh punches this off the back foot towards the off side.
Slightly shorter and quicker on middle. Pooja Vastrakar works it towards square leg for a single.
Pooja Vastrakar is the new batter. She stroked a 59-ball 67 against Pakistan Women at this venue and India Women once again need her to step up.

OUT! LBW! Now, Sophie Ecclestone strikes and this is a big blow to India. The set Smriti Mandhana departs now and India are in big trouble. This one lands on a fuller length around off and turns into Smriti Mandhana. She looks to sweep it but misses. The ball hits her pads and there is an appeal. The umpire raises his finger but Smriti Mandhana reviews. The replays roll in and the UltraEdge shows no bat involved. The Ball Tracking rolls and it shows that the impact is with the umpire's call and the ball is hitting the stumps. So the original decision stays and Smriti Mandhana walks back disappointed.

DRS time! The finger has gone up after an appeal for an lbw against Smriti Mandhana. She has reviewed the decision. A massive moment in the match. Nothing on the UltraEdge. Ball Tracking finds the impact with the umpire's call and it's going on to hit the wickets. The onfield decision remains as it is and India Women have now lost their 6th wicket.
Slightly shorter on off. Smriti Mandhana goes back and defends it.
A flatter delivery on off. Smriti Mandhana blocks this off the front foot.
FOUR! Smriti Mandhana gets the boundary and this will ease some pressure! This is tossed up on off. Smriti Mandhana skips down the track and lifts this over mid off for a boundary.
This time she goes slower on off. Ghosh drives but gets a thick outside edge to short third man. 10 dots in a row for Richa Ghosh who will be feeling the heat. She is a free-flowing batter by nature.
This time it is quicker and flatter, around off. Ghosh is stuck on her crease and looks to push at it but gets beaten.
This is another loopy delivery on off. Ghosh drives it to mid off again.
Slower in the air, on off. Ghosh drives it to mid off.
Tossed up on middle. Smriti Mandhana uses her feet and takes it on full and drives it to mid off for a single.
Dean serves this fuller on off. Smriti Mandhana pushes it to covers.
Slower through the air, landing full and around off, Ghosh drives but finds mid off. Maiden!
Floated one, full and on middle, Ghosh flicks but finds the fielder at short mid-wicket.
Quicker and full, around leg, it's eased down to mid on.
Slower through the air, short and close to off, Ghosh goes back to cut but misses.
Fuller this time, around off, driven down to mid off.
Floated delivery, landing full and on middle, Ghosh goes on the back foot in defense.
Same line and same length but this time Ghosh drives it well, through the gap at covers for a single.
Too full and around off, Richa Ghosh drives it down to mid off.
Loopy and full around off, Smriti Mandhana drives it through covers for a single.
Presses forward and drives a full ball to extra cover. Dot again.
Serves it a bit short, around off, Mandhana goes back and eases it to backward point. A good diving stop there.
Flighted and full, around off, Smriti Mandhana lunges and defends it to covers.
Tossed up, full and on off, Richa Ghosh pushes it down to mid off. Tidy stuff.
Flighted and full around off, Richa Ghosh pushes it through covers and opens her account with a couple of runs.
Loopy one this time, full and around off, Ghosh drives it down to mid off.
Fires in a full ball on off, Ghosh defends it off the front foot.
A bit short again, around off and turning in, Mandhana goes back and works it through square leg for a run.
Flatter and shorter around off, Smriti Mandhana goes back and pushes it to cover-point.
A touch short and on off, it's defended off the back foot. A double-wicket maiden for Charlotte Dean!
Full and around off, Richa pushes it to covers.
Richa Ghosh is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Charlotte Dean is on a roll. The Indian batsmen love their cover drives and falling in an attempt to do that. This is the carbon copy of the last dismissal. Charlotte Dean cleverly tosses it up and lands it full outside off, enticing the drive. This lands and straightens, Sneh Rana tries to play an expansive drive through the line but all she manages is an outside edge. Amy Jones catches, appeals and the finger is up. India Women staring down the barrel after losing half their side.
Commentary.Howout: c Amy Jones b Charlotte Dean

Commentary.Commentary: Full and flighted on off, driven to covers.
Sneh Rana walks in at number 6.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! This is a massive breakthrough for England Women as the dangerous Harmanpreet Kaur is on her way back to the pavilion. Charlotte Dean has done the magic in her first over itself. Serves it full and around off, this one lands and goes straight on, Harmanpreet Kaur leans forward, looking to defend with the spin. But it skids off the surface, collects a thin outside edge and Amy Jones grabs an excellent reflex catch. They appeal and Harmanpreet Kaur starts to walk. The finger is up as well. England Women back on top!
Commentary.Howout: c Amy Jones b Charlotte Dean

Commentary.Commentary: Starts with a tossed-up delivery, a full toss around off, Kaur pushes it to covers.
Charlotte Dean comes into the attack now.
Full and flighted on off, Mandhana drives it down the ground but finds mid off.
Well stopped! Short in length and outside off, Smriti Mandhana goes back and cracks it through the line. The point fielder dives across to her right to stop the racing ball.
Soft hands. Kaur gently tucks it towards mid-wicket and steals a single.
A touch short and on off, Smriti Mandhana goes back and works it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Advances down the track to take it on the full but drives it straight to covers.
Serves it short and on middle, Harmanpreet Kaur goes back and pulls it behind square leg for a single.
Shorter length, on middle and it comes slower off the pitch. Smriti Mandhana is early on the pull and mistimes it towards mid-wicket.
Back of a length, around off. Smriti Mandhana pushes it towards the off side.
WIDE! This is fuller but down the leg side. Smriti Mandhana looks to clip it but misses.
Goes shorter on middle and leg. Kaur looks to pull it but the ball comes slower than she expected and goes off her body to fine leg. A leg bye is taken.
Tight line again, on a length and around off. Kaur blocks this off the front foot.
Another length delivery, around off. Kaur defends this off the front foot towards the off side.
A length delivery, on off at 97 kph. Smriti Mandhana pushes it towards covers for a single.

Drinks break. Early hiccups for India Women and they are trying to revive their innings through the stand between Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana. These two are the in-form batters and India won't mind them playing out the maximum overs. For England Women, it is all about maintaining the same pressure and not allowing the momentum to slip away. So far, the defending champions have been right on the money, especially with their catching and ground fielding, and would look to continue the same. The middle phase is going to be decisive.
Tossed up nicely again, on off. Kaur defends this off the front foot again. Good start by Sophie Ecclestone.
Flighted delivery on off. Kaur puts a big stride forward and blocks it.
Nicely bowled! Slower on middle, Kaur defends it towards the leg side off the front foot.
Fuller and slower again, on off. Smriti Mandhana pushes it towards cover-point for a single.
This time she goes fuller on middle. Smriti Mandhana works it towards the leg side.
Slightly shorter and quicker to start, on off. Smriti Mandhana defends it towards the off side.
Change in bowling. Anya Shrubsole (6-1-20-2) gets a breather and in comes Sophie Ecclestone into the attack.
On a length, around off. Kaur punches it towards the off side this time.

THREE WIDES! Again down the leg side. Kaur looks to clip it away but misses. The keeper is upto the stumps and misses it too. The ball goes towards the fine leg region again and Tammy Beaumont stops it with a dive. The batters run two as the umpire stretches the arms.
This time drifting on the pads. Kaur clips it fine towards the fine leg region. Tammy Beaumont in the deep runs to her right and stops it. Two runs taken and 50 up for India.
FOUR! Lovely shot this time and shows the kind of form she is in. This is overpitched around off. Kaur leans forward and creams it through covers for a boundary.
A good-length delivery, around off at 98 kph. Kaur is well forward and defends this one to covers.
On a length, on middle and leg. Kaur works it towards the leg side.
Goes fuller on off, Smriti Mandhana drives it to mid off for a single.
Another length delivery, on off. Kaur blocks this solidly off the front foot.

FOUR! Another good delivery but this time a boundary for India. A good-length delivery, around off. Kaur pushes forward to defend. She does so with soft hands as the ball catches the outside edge of her blade. It goes past the slip fielder through the third man region for a boundary.
This is fuller on off. Kaur drives it to mid on this time.
On a length, on off. Kaur defends it towards point.
A good-length delivery, around off. Kaur pushes forward to defend but the ball beats the outside edge of her blade.

A huge appeal from the bowler but it is pitching outside leg. This is around leg, on a length. Smriti Mandhana looks to clip it away but misses. The ball hits her pads and goes towards the leg side. A leg bye is taken. No review was taken.
Just two from the over! A length delivery, on off. Kaur is solid in her front-foot defence.
A length delivery, on middle and leg. Smriti Mandhana works it to the left of square leg for a single.
A length delivery, on off. Smriti Mandhana defends it watchfully towards the off side.
A fullish delivery on off. Smriti Mandhana drives again towards covers but fails to find the gap again.
A full delivery again, on off at 103 kph. Smriti Mandhana drives it to covers.
Goes fuller on middle. Kaur works it to the right of mid on for a single.
Powerplay 2 time. A maximum of 4 fielders are now allowed outside the ring till the 40th over.
A leg-stump half-volley, Smriti Mandhana whips it to deep square leg for a couple. At the end of Powerplay 1, India Women are at 37/3!
Wide! Slips a length ball down the leg side, Mandhana tries to flick but misses.
FOUR! Finds the gap! Fuller in length and outside off, Smriti Mandhana presses forward and threads the gap at covers for a boundary.
Fractionally short and around off, Mandhana punches it from the crease but finds the cover fielder. Dot balls creating pressure.
On middle and off, around good length, Smriti Mandhana defends it from the back foot.
Smriti Mandhana plays the cover drive this time but fails to pierce the gap.
On a length and around off, Smriti Mandhana stays on the back foot and pushes it to cover-point.
Angles in a full ball around off, Kaur drives it back to the bowler. 2 from Sciver's first over!
Back of a length, around middle, it's pulled behind square leg for a single.
Fullish and on off, Smriti Mandhana drives but finds mid off.
A touch too straight and it's worked towards square leg for a run.
Full again, outside off, Kaur is forward and pushes it to point.
Fuller in length and outside off, Harmanpreet Kaur gets forward and defends it to covers.
Harmanpreet Kaur is the next batter in. Here is the first bowling change of the game as Natalie Sciver replaces Katherine Brunt.

OUT! Sharma is run out! This England team is pumped up! After a few days of soul-searching, the reigning champions are all charged up in the field. They have started like a house on fire. Fuller delivery, around off, Deepti Sharma drives it straight to mid off and attempts for a risky single. Kate Cross attacks the ball, picks it up and knocks the stumps down at the bowler's end. Deepti Sharma has given up already and the onfield umpire raises the finger. Those dot balls really played a part in this wicket. The third wicket goes down for India Women and they are under some early pressure.
Play and a miss! Width on offer outside off, Deepti Sharma throws her bat at it but fails to connect.
Around off, defended safely.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
Wide! Sliding down the leg side, on a fuller length, Sharma leaves it.
On a good length and around off, Deepti Sharma stays back and pushes it away to the off side. Not in the gap.
Full and around off, Deepti drives but finds the fielder at covers.
Pitches it up and around off, Smriti drives it past the diving extra cover fielder but the mid off fielder has it covered. Another top over from England Women!
Fuller and on middle, Smriti Mandhana closes the face of her bat and helps it to mid-wicket.
Stays on the back foot and pushes it defensively to point.
Sliding down the leg side, Smriti Mandhana fails to flick and it goes behind off her pads. The keeper collects it to her right.
Good timing and placement this time as Smriti Mandhana sends it through cover-point and collects a couple of runs.
Back of a length, around off and angling away, Mandhana pushes it with an angled bat to point.
Fuller this time, around off, blocked by Sharma. A wicket maiden from Anya Shrubsole!
Around off, on a length and shaping away, Deepti defends it from the crease.
That is defended solidly off the front foot.
On a good length around middle, Deepti Sharma defends it from the back foot.
Deepti Sharma is the next batter in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Excellently done by Sophia Dunkley. England Women have been blamed for their catching and ground fielding and this catch would do a world of good to their confidence.​ Anya Shrubsole puts it on a fuller length outside off, Mithali Raj leans forward to drive but only manages to slice it in the air at cover-point. Sophia Dunkley is manning that region, she goes down quickly and snaps it inches above the surface. They are claiming the catch, Smriti Mandhana asks her skipper to wait and the umpires take it upstairs. The soft signal is out and it will stay out after watching the replay. Sophia Dunkley has her hands wrapped under the ball. Big blow to India Women!
Commentary.Howout: c Sophia Dunkley b Anya Shrubsole

Commentary.Commentary: Is that taken? England Women are claiming the catch. The umpires have referred it upstairs. Soft signal is out.
Fuller in length and around off, Mithali Raj drives but finds mid off.

NOT OUT! The Indian skipper is off the mark! Length delivery on off. Raj looks to defends off the front foot. The ball goes off the inside half of her blade towards backward square leg and a slight mix-up between the batters. Smriti Mandhana though is quick and completes the run despite a direct hit at the striker's end. The replays confirm the same.
No real appeal for a run out. Polite enquiries only after a direct hit at the striker's end. The square leg umpire plays safe and takes it upstairs. Smriti Mandhana is safe.
Shorter length and around leg. Smriti Mandhana pulls it to deep square leg for a single.
A length delivery, around off. Smriti Mandhana pushes it towards cover-point.
This time the ball holds on the surface a little. Fullish delivery on off. Smriti Mandhana checks her drive at the last moment and hits this one towards mid off.
Goes fuller on off this time. Smriti Mandhana drives it to covers.
WIDE! This is on a length and down the leg side this time. Smriti Mandhana looks to work it away but misses. The umpire calls it wide.
FOUR! Smriti Mandhana takes advantage of a poor delivery this time! Back of a length, on middle and leg. Smriti Mandhana pulls it towards the backward square leg region for a boundary.
This is on a length, on off. Raj defends but gets the inside edge onto her pads this time. End of a brilliant over from Anya Shrubsole!
Beaten! This is on a good length and around off. Raj pushes forward to defend but the ball beats the outside edge of her blade as it moves away from her.
Skipper Mithali Raj walks in next.

OUT! Drags it on! Anya Shrubsole continues to dominate against the left-handers and provides the first breakthrough - her 100th wicket in ODIs! She lands it on a good length, around off at 106 kph and it has a hint of inswing there. Bhatia leans forward to drive but gets a thin inside edge as the ball goes behind to disturb the stumps. So India Women lose an early wicket and England Women would look to capitalise on this start.
She goes fuller this time on off. Smriti Mandhana drives it towards mid off. Cross moves swiftly towards her left and stops it. A single taken.
Tighter line and length this time. On a length and close to off. Smriti Mandhana blocks it out.
FOUR! Now Smriti Mandhana joins the act! This is full on off. Smriti Mandhana drives it through covers for a lovely boundary.
On a length and angling into middle and leg. Bhatia works it towards the deep backward square leg region for a couple. 7 from the over, a good one for India Women!

FOUR! Impressive timing! This time on a length, on middle. Bhatia works it through mid-wicket and beats the diving fielders (at mid-wicket and mid on) with supreme timing. First boundary of the innings.
Brunt targets the stumps this time. Bhatia works this length delivery towards mid-wicket.
A length delivery, around off. Bhatia defends it towards the off side.
Mid off goes a little wider, more towards extra cover.
Goes fuller on off. Bhatia drives it to mid off.
A length delivery on middle this time. Smriti Mandhana works it towards the leg side, finds square leg.
This time she finds the gap and will keep the strike with a single. A length delivery, around off. Smriti Mandhana steers it past the diving point fielder and takes a single.
This time she pulls her length back a little, on off. Smriti Mandhana defends it towards cover-point.
Goes fuller again, on off. Smriti Mandhana drives with good timing again but finds the fielder at cover-point once more.
Fullish again, around off. Smriti Mandhana drives it to cover-point.
This time a bit straighter, on middle and full again. Smriti Mandhana drives it towards the leg side this time, finds mid on.

Beautiful drive! This is full, on off. Smriti Mandhana leans forward and drives it through covers. The fielder from the ring runs behind it and cuts it off with a slide near the fence. Two runs are taken. A bit lazy running between the wickets.
Anya Shrubsole to bowl from the opposite end. Two slips in place.
Another delivery on that tight line! A length delivery, on off. Bhatia defends this watchfully. Decent start by Brunt.
This is better as she serves this full on off. Bhatia drives it back to the bowler.
On a length and around off. Bhatia drives it to the cover fielder in the ring.
Another delivery, around off and it is slightly fuller this time. Bhatia pushes it through covers and gets a couple.
A length delivery, around off. Bhatia punches it to cover-point.

Almost a mix-up off the first ball! This is on a length, on leg. Smriti Mandhana looks to clip but misses. The ball hits her pads and goes towards the leg side. Bhatia calls for a run but Smriti Mandhana is late to respond but finally takes a run as the fielder misses the throw at the bowler's end. A leg bye is taken. The replays show that Smriti Mandhana would have been a goner in case of a direct hit.
Ready to go, finally! Smriti Mandhana on strike...

All in readiness here at the Bay Oval. The English players get into a quick huddle before spreading on the field. Out come the openers of India Women - Smriti Mandhana and Yastika Bhatia. The players take a moment to extend their support to the Black Lives Matter movement. Katherine Brunt to bowl the first over. Slight delay before the first ball. Not sure about the reason yet. Nasser Hussain (on air) informs that one of the players is slightly ill before the start. The groundstaff is also out there to clear one part of the field.

Time for the anthems! The players from both groups are out there and lining up for the same. It's a relief to have bright and sunny conditions - the setting is perfect to play this crunch game. To be honest, the current conditions are looking ripe for batting and the decision from England Women to bowl first here could be a point of debate later on if they don't perform with the ball.

Harmanpreet Kaur is down for a quick chat. On her performance in the World Cup, she says that it is a great achievement for her (scoring three WC tons) and she wants to be greedy now and is looking to do better. She adds that sometimes you struggle with injuries and other things but it is important to bounce back. Mentions that they did well in the last game and they want to do the same thing today and improve on the aspects they can.
Pitch report - No scratches on the pitch and it will mostly stay the same. It's a new wicket and has similar features to the other ones. It's dry and the seam bowlers will have to work really hard.

India Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Yastika Bhatia, Mithali Raj (C), Deepti Sharma, Harmanpreet Kaur, Richa Ghosh (WK), Pooja Vastrakar, Jhulan Goswami, Sneh Rana, Meghna Singh, Rajeshwari Gayakwad.

England Women (Unchanged Playing XI) - Tammy Beaumont, Danni Wyatt, Heather Knight (C), Natalie Sciver, Amy Jones (WK), Sophia Dunkley, Katherine Brunt, Kate Cross, Sophie Ecclestone, Charlotte Dean, Anya Shrubsole.

Mithali Raj, the skipper of India Women, says that they would have batted first and as Knight said it is on the drier side. She informs that they are going with the unchanged XI. She mentions that they are looking to be consistent and says that it is a positive for this team that they have played T20 World Cup final. Tells that lot of players have also played the Big Bash League and that gives them experience and it is a positive thing for them.

Heather Knight, the captain of England Women, says that it's a fresh pitch and they want to bowl and it might be on the drier side. Wants to keep India Women down to a reasonable total. Informs that they are unchanged. Adds that they have been very close to winning all those games and feels that they have the skills. Mentions that there is pressure but they are still in it 100 per cent, and they are looking to do well in this match.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of England Women. They have elected to BOWL first.

India Women, on the other hand, will be high on confidence after their clinical performance against Windies in the last encounter. Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur displayed their class in the last game and India will hope that they can continue in the same vein. The strike rate of other batters remains a concern though along with Indian seamers' performance with the new ball. These are some key issues India need to address if they want to go deep in the tournament and a strong performance against this English unit will give them a lot of confidence. Can India hand England their fourth loss of the tournament? Or will England finally register their first win of this World Cup? We shall find out soon. Toss and team sheets in a while.

England Women were one of the pre-tournament favourites along with Australia Women but unfortunately for the English fans, they have failed to live up to the billing. Yes, they have lost three close games but one expects an experienced team like England to win crucial moments in the game. Their top order has failed to deliver in the last two games while their bowling has also lacked penetration, especially their experienced seam attack. It remains to be seen how they go about their business with their back against the wall.

It is time for the finalists of the previous edition of the ICC Women’s World Cup to lock horns as England Women take on India Women in this crucial game number 15. The defending champions are under the pump as they have lost all three games so far and are in desperate need of a win here. India, on the other hand, will know that a win against a strong English side will be a big boost in their bid to qualify for the semis. A mouth-watering contest awaits us. On that note, welcome to our coverage.
